description: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across different layers of a large language model, using a threshold of 1e-3 to define sparsity. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5, indicating a linear scale representing the depth of the model’s transformer layers. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.8, also on a linear scale, and quantifies the proportion of attention weights below the threshold. Three distinct lines are plotted: a blue dashed line representing the sparsity ratio before gating, which remains consistently near zero (average 0.003) across all layers; an orange dotted line for the sparsity ratio after gating, which starts near 0.8 at layer 0, drops sharply to below 0.2 by layer 5, and then gradually declines to near 0.02 by layer 20 before slightly fluctuating; and a green dash-dotted line for the sparsity ratio after average gating, which begins near 0.8 at layer 0, falls steeply to around 0.1 by layer 5, and continues to decrease to near 0.01 by layer 20, remaining low thereafter. The legend provides the average sparsity ratios for each condition, highlighting the significant increase in sparsity induced by gating mechanisms compared to the pre-gate state.
